evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. fabrīlis: scalprum (Liv. 27.49.1), opera (Verg. A. 8.415)
terms.comment: A description of ours: mēnsa, a table for any purpose, with fabrīlis, of a craftsman (scalprum fabrīle, a carpenter’s chisel). We have found no ancient word for a workbench in Lewis & Short, and none in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini.

phrases.english: Put the plank on the workbench.

phrases.latin: Ferrāmenta in mēnsā fabrīlī nē relinquās; in arcam repōne.
phrases.english: Don’t leave the tools on the workbench; put them back in the box.

sources: Lewis & Short: mensa · Lewis & Short: fabrilis
